title: Transsexual's death during arrest ruled an accident
article: Whether the person who died was a woman or a man may still be open to debate, but a coroner's jury ruled yesterday the death was an accident.
The jury found that Abdirhman Ali Abdi, who was known on the streets of Hamilton by the female identity Chevranna, died after choking on vomit brought on by cocaine poisoning.
An inquest is mandatory whenever someone dies in police custody.
The jury opted to make no recommendations aimed at preventing another death in similar circumstances.
Abdi, a 26-year-old transsexual and intravenous drug user, went into cardiac arrest at about 9:20 p.m. on Feb. 20, 2003.
That was about 10 minutes after she had run screaming from an eighth-floor apartment of a Sanford Avenue North building.
With her long brown hair pulled back in a ponytail, Abdi was holding a broom in one hand and a knife in the other and shouting incoherently about being chased by dogs and bikers.
Other tenants tried to help the delusional woman and one man managed to wrestle the knife away. George Draper suffered several bites in the process.
He later learned Abdi was HIV positive and has himself continued to be tested every five or six months.
Police arrested Abdi and carried her down seven floors of stairs because elevators were out of order. Once in the front lobby, they discovered she was not breathing and had no pulse.

Marco Visentini, the lawyer for Hamilton Police Service, argued that Abdi, who resisted arrest by kicking and flailing, had essentially been treated with kid gloves by the tenants and uniformed officers involved.
"The officers responded with the appropriate level of force. There was no evidence of excessive force by anyone," said Visentini.

Coroner's counsel James Ramsay said police, firefighters and paramedics, who carried out advanced cardiac life support in the vestibule, were swift and thorough in their efforts to resuscitate Abdi. Nonetheless, the patient was pronounced dead at Hamilton General Hospital at 10:20 p.m.
"Medically speaking, (Abdi) had every break, but it doesn't always work," said Ramsay.
